newsitem.title: FRANCE: "Money laundering" takes on new meaning in France.
newsitem.headline: "Money laundering" takes on new meaning in France.

text.p: France's underworld has apparently taken to laundering money -- literally rather than through foreign bank accounts -- to foil authorities trying to track down stolen cash, justice sources said on Friday.

The sources said three men in their 50s were in custody in Ajaccio on the Mediterranean island of Corsica on suspicion of using a home-made cocktail of cleaning products to launder indelible security ink from 100 and 200 franc banknotes stolen in a raid on an armoured car in July.
Justice officials declined to disclose the mixture's ingredients, but they said the men were also suspected of involvement in several other money thefts.
The system of marking bills with the ink, intended to discourage thieves by making the notes easily recognisable, was put in place by the Bank of France, the French central bank.

The three men were alleged to have set up their laundry in an aircraft hangar in Cuttoli Corticchiato, 30 km (20 miles) north of Ajaccio. Investigators said they believed the trio were not involved in the actual hold-up in July and police were still looking for the thieves.
